security_audit.summary: All 176 static findings are false positives caused by Markdown formatting, illustrative paths, and a bounded Graphviz rendering utility. No command injection, path traversal, hidden-file access, reconnaissance, or scheduled execution was found. However, the guidance deliberately uses deception and persuasion to force model compliance, creating a high semantic risk.

remediation.issue: The references teach authority framing, forced choices, and deceptive scenarios that make agents believe tests are real.
remediation.suggestion: Replace coercive patterns with transparent evaluations that preserve agent judgment and prohibit fabricated authority, urgency, or consequences.

remediation.issue: The examples treat absolute compliance with skill text as the primary success measure.
remediation.suggestion: Require skills to yield to current user intent, safety policies, and verified project context; measure task quality instead of obedience.

content.user_title: Create and Test Reliable AI Skills
content.value_statement: AI skill documentation can be unclear, hard to discover, and untested. This guide provides structured authoring, discovery, testing, and refinement methods for reusable skills.
actual_capabilities: Structures SKILL.md files with YAML frontmatter, searchable descriptions, and concise sections.
Applies a RED-GREEN-REFACTOR workflow to skill authoring and revision.
Defines pressure scenarios for testing whether agents follow discipline-oriented guidance.
Explains naming, keyword coverage, token efficiency, cross-references, and file organization.
Provides Graphviz conventions and a Node.js utility for rendering DOT blocks as SVG files.
Includes Anthropic authoring guidance and examples for validating skill documentation.
limitations: Requires access to subagents for the full pressure-testing workflow.
The rendering utility requires Node.js and a local Graphviz dot executable.
The compliance-focused guidance can encourage rigid or manipulative prompts without careful review.
It does not provide an automated test harness or marketplace publishing integration.

use_cases.title: Create a new AI skill
use_cases.description: Build a concise skill with clear triggers, focused guidance, useful examples, and a validation plan.

use_cases.title: Improve an existing skill
use_cases.description: Refine discovery metadata, remove unnecessary content, close documented gaps, and repeat targeted behavior tests.

use_cases.title: Standardize skill quality
use_cases.description: Define shared authoring conventions, review criteria, test scenarios, and deployment checks across a skill library.

prompt_templates.title: Draft a basic skill
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a SKILL.md for [topic]. Define clear triggers, a concise overview, one core pattern, common mistakes, and a practical example.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when starting a focused skill from a proven technique.

prompt_templates.title: Improve discovery metadata
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this skill name and description. Rewrite them for concrete triggers, search keywords, and concise third-person language without summarizing the workflow.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when agents do not discover or load an existing skill reliably.

prompt_templates.title: Design a test campaign
prompt_templates.prompt: Create three transparent pressure scenarios for this discipline-focused skill. Include baseline and enabled runs, success criteria, expected rationalizations, and an iteration plan.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when validating whether guidance remains useful under realistic constraints.

prompt_templates.title: Audit and refactor a skill suite
prompt_templates.prompt: Assess these related skills for overlap, discovery gaps, token cost, unsafe authority language, cross-reference quality, and test coverage. Propose a prioritized revision plan.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when maintaining a mature library with shared standards and dependencies.

output_examples.input: Create a skill for diagnosing flaky tests.
output_examples.output: A concise skill outline with race-condition triggers, a condition-based waiting pattern, one focused example, common mistakes, and validation scenarios.

output_examples.input: Review this skill description for discoverability.
output_examples.output: A trigger-focused description that names observable symptoms, avoids workflow details, and includes terms an agent is likely to search.

output_examples.input: Plan tests for a verification skill.
output_examples.output: A transparent baseline, three constrained scenarios, measurable quality criteria, likely failure modes, and a revision sequence.

best_practices: Run a baseline test before changing a skill, then repeat the same scenario after each revision.
Keep descriptions focused on activation conditions and place workflow details in the skill body.
Use transparent test scenarios and preserve user authority when evaluating agent behavior.
anti_patterns: Do not treat model obedience as the only measure of skill quality.
Do not use fabricated emergencies, authority, or personal consequences to force compliance.
Do not add large references or tools unless they support a repeated workflow.

faq.question: What does this skill help create?
faq.answer: It helps create and revise reusable AI skill documentation with clear triggers, focused guidance, examples, and validation steps.

faq.question: Does it work with Claude and Codex?
faq.answer: Yes. The guidance targets Claude, Codex, and Claude Code skill formats and workflows.

faq.question: Does it generate an automated test harness?
faq.answer: No. It explains manual and subagent testing methods, but the repository only lists a harness as future work.

faq.question: How are flowcharts rendered?
faq.answer: A Node.js utility extracts DOT blocks from SKILL.md and uses the local Graphviz dot command to generate SVG files.

faq.question: Must every skill use pressure testing?
faq.answer: No. The guide recommends pressure testing mainly for discipline-oriented skills where agents may bypass costly rules.

faq.question: What security concern should authors consider?
faq.answer: Avoid deceptive or coercive prompts. Skill guidance must remain subordinate to user intent, safety policies, and verified project context.
